source: Academic-Regulations-2023.pdf, hand-encoded from direct reading, not regex-parsed - guessing rule meaning from free-text prose is exactly what the brief warns against.
note_on_terminology: CDC/DEL/HUEL/OPEL are bulletin/campus shorthand, not terms these regulations define. Confirmed by their absence: clauses 2.04-2.06 spell out 'Discipline-specific Core courses', 'Discipline Electives', 'Humanities Electives', 'Open Electives' in full, never the abbreviations.

named_courses.description: For first degree students, named courses include all mandatory courses under the General Institutional Requirement and the Discipline-specific Core courses for the programme(s).

open_elective.description: Courses that are not part of the discipline requirement nor part of the Humanities requirement.

elective_substitution_rule.description: Normally any elective course will be treated as an Open Elective once the student's requirements under Discipline Electives and Humanities Electives have been accounted for.
elective_substitution_rule.dual_degree_note: Open elective requirement of dual degree students is met by counting the Discipline Electives of one degree as Open Electives of the other degree - stated directly at clause 2.06, a cleaner one-line statement of the same rule 7.11-7.12 describe in more detail for the composite programme.

higher_degree_elective_option.description: A first degree student above a particular CGPA (set by AGC) may register in at most one higher-degree course per semester, counted as Open Elective unless it happens to be listed in their own programme's Discipline Elective pool.
higher_degree_elective_option.engine_relevance: This is why higher-degree (G-series) handout course codes are NOT included in this project's default Open Elective candidate pool - the CGPA gate can't be checked (student profile doesn't collect CGPA), so the safe default is exclusion, not silent inclusion.

prerequisite_policy.default_rule: positional, but three distinct cases - not one blanket rule

ps_1.description: Prior preparation for PS-I = normally all courses in the semesters preceding PS-I for the student's programme or composite programme.

ps_2_or_ts.description: Prior preparation for PS-II/Thesis = ALL named courses of the programme or composite programme, including PS-I, other than TS/PS-II itself. This is broader than 'preceding semesters' - it means the entire named-course list, not just what came before.

any_other_semester.description: For any other prescribed semester, prior preparation = all named courses in semesters and terms preceding this set of courses. This is the case the requirement engine's positional gating actually implements.

dca_flexibility.condition: The uncleared courses must have no direct bearing on Core courses. DCA may recommend a modified semester-wise pattern; finalization is at the discretion of Dean, AUGS/AGSR.

prerequisite_policy.known_gap: No course-to-course pairwise prerequisite list (e.g. 'course X requires course Y') found anywhere in the supplied dataset - checked in these regulations, the bulletin's course-pool section, and the timetable's own dedicated 'Prerequisites/Restrictions' section (which turned out to be a stub pointing to an external website, not data). Positional prerequisite enforcement per the three cases above is the only rule implemented.

ps_i_ps_ii.description: PS-I (5 units) then PS-II (20 units). PS-I normally after prior preparation from the semester-wise pattern; PS-II only after all named courses (including PS-I) of the programme are cleared.

thesis_16_units.description: 16-unit Thesis, full semester duration. Student cannot be simultaneously registered in any other course.

thesis_9_units.description: 9-unit Thesis with concurrent coursework (at most 3 courses, at most 9 units total, normally accounted under Open Electives).

modified_open_elective_requirement.single_degree_9_unit_thesis: At least 2 additional elective courses (at least 6 units) - modified Open Elective requirement becomes at least 7 courses / at least 21 units. A completed PS-I's units may count toward this.
modified_open_elective_requirement.dual_degree_one_9_unit_thesis: Modified Open Elective requirement (>=7 courses / >=21 units) is deemed satisfied if the combined Discipline Electives from both programmes already exceed that threshold; otherwise additional electives are needed.
modified_open_elective_requirement.dual_degree_both_9_unit_thesis: Modified requirement becomes >=9 courses / >=27 units, satisfiable by combined Discipline Electives from both programmes plus a completed PS-I if applicable.

practice_school_thesis_rule.implemented_for: single degree only - dual degree logic documented here, not yet built into the engine

minor_program_rules.declaration_deadline: End of 2nd year (later declaration may delay the minor's award, subject to course availability)
minor_program_rules.requirement: Each minor defines its own minimum courses/units, a set of mandatory core courses, and an elective pool. At most 1 project/seminar-type course may count toward a minor's elective requirement.

overlap_rule.major_course_overlap_cap: At most 2 courses AND at most 6 units (out of the minor's 5-course/15-unit requirement) may be met by the student's major's mandatory courses - specifically General Institutional Requirement excluding Humanities, or (Major) Discipline Core(s).
overlap_rule.elective_overlap: No cap - major electives (discipline/open/humanities) may overlap freely with minor elective requirements.
overlap_rule.no_double_counting: No course may satisfy two different minors, nor may a course satisfy two majors and a minor simultaneously.

minor_certificate_eligibility.regulation_clause: 9.01 (attached directly after the main graduation clause, not a separate numbered clause)
conditions: Completed the core courses required for the minor and the stipulated number of electives from that minor's pool.
Minimum CGPA of 4.50 in the courses applied toward the minor.
minor_certificate_eligibility.issued_only_after: A minor certificate is issued only on completion of the major degree - a student can graduate without a minor, but not with only a minor.

minor_program_rules.implemented: documented only - student profile has a minor field, but the engine doesn't consume it yet

conditions: Cleared all courses prescribed for the programme or composite programme.
Cleared total unit requirements of Thesis, Seminar and Dissertation wherever applicable.
Minimum CGPA 4.50 (first degree) or 5.50 (higher degree, unless stated otherwise for a particular programme).
Remained outside the purview of the Academic Counselling Board (ACB), or declared outside its purview.

Overcome all consequential stipulations of any NC report - EXCEPT an NC in an elective course beyond the prescribed number of electives, or in a course that has ceased to be part of the student's current programme after a transfer.
Satisfied all other requirements of these regulations.

eligibility_gating.description: Which programme pairs are eligible for dual degree is NOT defined in these regulations - it's explicitly deferred to 'Groups of programmes... notified in the bulletin as per periodic decision of the Senate' (clause 2.03). No separate abstract 'Groups' table was found; the operational definition used by this project is: a combination is valid if and only if the bulletin publishes a named composite semester-wise pattern for it.

composite_programme_principles.gir_counted_once: General Institutional Requirement is shared, not duplicated per degree.
composite_programme_principles.discipline_requirements: Met separately per degree, except courses common to both (or marked equivalent), which need be completed only once.
composite_programme_principles.no_double_dipping: A Discipline Core course of one degree cannot count as a Discipline Elective of the other; no course counts as Discipline Elective in two disciplines.
composite_programme_principles.open_elective_subsumed: See elective_substitution_rule.dual_degree_note above - stated at both 2.06 and 7.11.
composite_programme_principles.ps_thesis_choice: Exactly one of: 2 PS-II courses, 2 Thesis courses, or 1 PS-II + 1 Thesis. Choice expressed after completing PS-I, within one semester; Dean PS decides if the student doesn't.
composite_programme_principles.all_or_nothing_graduation: The composite programme can't be completed separately per degree - completing it fulfils both degrees at once, same division/class awarded to both.

restrictions.no_dropping_first_degree: A dual degree student cannot drop the first degree and keep only the second.
restrictions.withdrawal: Reverts the student to their first single degree, subject to current structure and regulations.
